name: Cha Bum-kun
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest player in the world to reach 100 international caps at age 24 in 1978, won Asian Games gold medal in 1978, and signed with Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga in July 1979 at age 26, later winning the UEFA Cup in 1980.
early_history_summary: Cha began playing football at Kyungshin Middle School and was selected for the South Korean U20 team in 1970 at age 17. He made his senior international debut for South Korea in 1972 at age 18, the youngest debutant at the time. By 1978, he had 100-plus caps and an Asian Games gold medal, before moving to Eintracht Frankfurt in 1979 where he scored 12 goals in his first Bundesliga season and helped win the UEFA Cup.
family_context_summary: Born in Hwaseong, South Korea. Originally joined Yeongdo Middle School to learn football but transferred to Kyungshin Middle School. No family financial or football background documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Korean national team pipeline, university football, early international debut, Bundesliga pioneer, high school mentor
evidence_summary: Cha was selected for the South Korean U20 team at 17 and made his senior international debut at 18, the youngest at the time. He reached 100 international caps by age 24, a world record, and won Asian Games gold in 1978 before signing with Eintracht Frankfurt at 26. His high school manager Chang Woon-soo helped him persist through difficulties with older students' violence. No family financial or domain background is documented. His trajectory reflects early specialization in Korea's national team pipeline and a pioneering move to European football.

name: Tim Berners-Lee

family_context_summary: Born in London to mathematicians and computer scientists Mary Lee Berners-Lee and Conway Berners-Lee, who both worked on the Ferranti Mark 1, the first commercially built computer. Brother Mike is a professor of ecology and climate change management.

name: Anni-Frid Lyngstad
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Swedish national talent competition 'New Faces' in September 1967 at age 21, securing an EMI recording contract and national TV exposure on Sweden's most popular show; released her first album 'Frida' in 1971 and scored a No. 1 Svensktoppen hit with 'Min egen stad' in October 1971 at age 25.

She released her first album 'Frida' in 1971, produced by Benny Andersson, with the single 'Min egen stad' reaching No. 1 on Svensktoppen in October 1971.
family_context_summary: Born to a Norwegian mother and German soldier father in post-war Norway; raised by her grandmother Arntine in Sweden after her mother died of kidney failure at age 21. Grew up in modest circumstances in Torshalla, where her grandmother worked as a seamstress.
parent_family_domain_summary: Grandmother sang Norwegian songs to her, fostering musical passion, but no family music industry connections or professional training documented.

name: Mike Oldfield
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album 'Tubular Bells' on 25 May 1973 at age 20, which became the first release on Virgin Records, sold over 2.7 million copies in the UK, reached No. 1 on the UK album chart, and was used in the film The Exorcist.
early_history_summary: Oldfield took up guitar at age 10, taught himself by copying Bert Jansch and John Renbourn records, and was performing in folk clubs by 11-12. He formed the folk duo the Sallyangie with his sister Sally in 1967, recording an album in 1969. He joined Kevin Ayers' band the Whole World in 1970, playing on two albums at Abbey Road Studios, before demoing Tubular Bells in 1971 and recording it for Virgin Records in 1972-73 at age 19.
family_context_summary: Born to Raymond Henry Oldfield, a general practitioner, and Maureen, an Irish nurse who developed barbiturate addiction and mental health problems. Father gave him his first guitar. Grew up in Reading, Berkshire, with elder siblings Sally and Terence, both also musicians. Left school at 15.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a GP who gave Oldfield his first guitar; sister Sally was his folk duo partner and brother Terry played flute in his band. No direct music industry family background, but siblings were musical collaborators.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught multi-instrumentalist, early folk club performance, Abbey Road access, Virgin Records launch, family adversity, obsessive concentration
evidence_summary: Oldfield taught himself guitar from age 10 by copying folk records and was performing in clubs by 11-12. He formed a folk duo with his sister Sally at 14, joined Kevin Ayers' band at 17 gaining access to Abbey Road Studios, and demoed Tubular Bells at 18. The album, recorded when he was 19 and released at 20, became the first Virgin Records release and sold over 2.7 million UK copies. His father, a GP, gave him his first guitar, but his mother's mental illness created a difficult home environment that he escaped through intense solitary music practice. His extraordinary multi-instrumental skill and obsessive concentration were the dominant early advantages.
